notes.text: Attaching a second statement to an occupied handle preserves the current statement and records the newcomer as supporting evidence. Replacing the current statement is a separate revision operation.

Access resolves a recalled atom through the handle's current statement and checks that the stored text matches the atom payload. A missing binding, missing or corrupt evidence, or a payload mismatch yields an issue and no returned text for that item.
SnapshotService copies the bytes exported by the supplied port and verifies by byte equality. A Core-only port therefore does not back up the separately stored statement files or handle bindings.

Retrying a write with the same statement ID and identical content leaves the stored statement intact. Reusing that ID with different content raises FileExistsError, so publish a revision under a new statement identity.

A Nollm memory statement carries an ID, meaningful text, an optional source handle, and zero or more context references. Its persisted mapping has exactly those four fields; a host can cite a Git source without changing Core.
